channel.title: Orphograph — Blog
channel.description: Notes from the office. Method, doctrine, and edge cases of Bitcoin-anchored timestamps.

item.title: How to date-stamp a document permanently
item.description: A plain-English guide to placing a permanent, third-party-verifiable date on a digital document — using a cryptographic fingerprint anchored to the Bitcoin chain, with no expiry and no trusted intermediary.

item.title: How to prove a contract existed before a date
item.description: A plain-English method for proving that a signed or unsigned contract existed in its present form before a specific calendar date. Anchor the document's cryptographic fingerprint to the Bitcoin chain and hold a third-party-verifiable date of record.

item.title: How to prove a photo was not edited
item.description: A plain-English guide to proving a photograph has not been edited since a specific moment, using a cryptographic fingerprint anchored to the Bitcoin chain. Verifiable by anyone, with no trusted intermediary.

item.title: How to prove a piece of code existed before a competitor's commit
item.description: A practical guide for engineers and engineering organisations: anchor a source tree's cryptographic fingerprint to the Bitcoin chain so a defensible date of record fixes the bytes before any competing commit. From the Orphograph office.

item.title: How to prove you created something before someone else
item.description: A plain-English method for establishing priority of creation — proving a draft, sketch, manuscript, or design existed in your hands before someone else's competing claim. Bitcoin-anchored, third-party-verifiable, permanent.

item.title: How to prove you wrote it — not an AI
item.description: A practical guide for writers, students, and journalists accused of using AI to produce text. Save the file, anchor its fingerprint to the Bitcoin chain, hold a verifiable date of record that pre-dates the accusation.

item.title: What makes a digital timestamp legally defensible
item.description: An institutional explainer of the properties that make a digital timestamp hold up under examination — independent verification, cryptographic binding, public anchoring, and continuity beyond the issuer. From the Orphograph office.

item.title: Why a Bitcoin block height is the strongest proof of existence in 2026
item.description: Why a Bitcoin block height is the strongest existence-proof anchor in 2026. Sixteen-year track record, attack costs, what would have to fail.

item.title: How Bitcoin merkle roots make file timestamps un-falsifiable
item.description: A technical walkthrough of why a timestamp anchored to Bitcoin is fundamentally different from a conventional database record. The math, the eight attacks an adversary would have to mount, and why each one fails in practice.

item.title: Digital notary vs cryptographic timestamp — what each one proves
item.description: Digital notary vs cryptographic timestamp — what each actually proves, why they are not interchangeable, and which one your use case needs.

item.title: How to prove a photo existed before an AI model was released
item.description: Step-by-step walkthrough to prove a photo existed before AI training. Bitcoin-anchored timestamp, free tier, ten-minute setup.

item.title: OpenTimestamps for non-developers — a 10-minute walkthrough
item.description: A practical explainer of what OpenTimestamps is, why it works, and how to use it without opening a terminal. Bitcoin-anchored proof of existence, with no per-record cost.

item.title: How to prove your photo existed before AI scraped it (without a lawyer)
item.description: A practical guide for photographers who want timestamp-grade proof of when they made an image. Bitcoin-anchored timestamps, free tier, ten-second workflow.

item.title: Reading an .ots file by hand — a forensic walkthrough
item.description: A byte-by-byte walkthrough of what is actually inside an OpenTimestamps proof file. For investigators, journalists verifying a tip, and anyone who wants to confirm the math is real.

item.title: Why Orphograph uses five OpenTimestamps calendars instead of one
item.description: Why submitting to five OpenTimestamps calendars instead of one matters — independent operators, no single point of failure, receipt survives outages.

item.title: Why your domain dying shouldn't kill your timestamp receipt
item.description: Most SaaS receipts are worthless when the company disappears. A Bitcoin-anchored timestamp is structurally different — the proof outlives the issuer by design.
